items.title: No eye-witnesses when Zara fell, Coroner's Court hears
items.summary: The investigating officer, Inspector Wong Yew Zhung, said no one, including security guards or hostel wardens, had patrolled the third floor of the hostel block where Zara Qairina stayed on the night of the incident. Wong said statements from students indicated that Zara Qairina was last seen by a group of students at about 10pm on July 15 when she was summoned by several Form Four students over an alleged theft. "Later that night, between 10.15pm and 10.30pm, several students from dormitory A-3-5 said they saw Zara enter the dormitory crying before lying down on the floor," he said.

items.title: Man seeking loan to help family ends up as account mule
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A man who sought a loan to help pay for his mother and sister's cancer treatment said he was under immense pressure after becoming an account mule. Izzuddin said he never received the money and decided to block his bank account a month later, only to discover five suspicious transactions. "Four transactions involved licensed moneylending scams, while another involved a car sale.

items.title: MCMC probes viral video over allegedly false, misleading Budget 2027 tax claims
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 13 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is examining a viral video alleged to contain false and misleading information regarding the Sales and Service Tax (SST) and income tax relief in the 2027 Budget. The MCMC said it has received public complaints regarding the video, which has been circulating on social media. According to the statement, the dissemination of such information could cause confusion regarding national taxation policies, trigger unfounded concerns, and influence the public’s financial decisions based on incorrect information.

items.title: Mexican man run over by ICE agents 'intentionally': Lawyer
items.summary: HOUSTON: Federal immigration agents in an unmarked SUV ran over a Mexican man during a pursuit in Texas, breaking his right leg in three places, his lawyer said Monday. ICE officals told Houston Public Media that Parra "ran in front of an ICE vehicle and was struck." ICE said they we seeking to detain Parra's passenger, who had a criminal record.

items.title: HLIB keeps 'Buy' call on MN Holdings, RM4.65 target
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has maintained its "Buy" call on MN Holdings Bhd with an unchanged target price of RM4.65, citing the company's strong positioning to benefit from Malaysia's accelerating power infrastructure investment cycle. The investment bank said MN Holdings' latest contract win to build power facilities for a data centre brought its year-to-date contract win for 2027 to RM643 million, representing 64 per cent of HLIB's RM1 billion full-year target for the company. "We remain positive on Malaysia's power infrastructure upcycle, with strong data centre and solar project pipelines driving demand for power infrastructure works from both private players and Tenaga.

items.title: Zara's mother refused post-mortem, investigating officer tells inquest
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The late Zara Qairina Mahathir's mother refused to allow a post-mortem examination despite receiving an explanation from police, the investigating officer told the Coroner's Court. Inspector Wong Yew Zhung said he met Noraidah Lamat at Queen Elizabeth Hospital (QEH) on July 17, 2025, after Zara Qairina, 13, was pronounced dead. "However, Zara's mother, refused to allow the post-mortem examination.

items.title: Police seek witnesses, dashcam footage after fatal Cheras-Kajang crash that killed motorcyclist
items.summary: Kajang police chief ACP Naazron Abdul Yusof said a report on the accident was received at about 6pm. He said preliminary investigations found that the victim, who was riding from Kuala Lumpur towards Kajang, is believed to have lost control before falling onto the road. He said the lorry driver has yet to lodge a police report.

items.title: Maran durian orchard operator loses RM202,460 in lottery scam
items.summary: Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the scam began on Nov 25 last year when the victim came across a Facebook video featuring a monk from southern Thailand who purportedly offered financial fortune-telling services. Azry said the agent demanded payments purportedly for bank processing fees and cross-border transfer taxes before releasing the winnings. The victim made 12 transactions totalling RM202,460 to six bank accounts between Dec 23 last year and May 22 this year.

items.title: Riyadh airport to remain shut until Oct 17 after deadly Houthi attacks
items.summary: RIYADH: Authorities have extended the closure of Riyadh's international airport until Saturday and airlines scrapped flights after continuing attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis emptied the skies over Saudi Arabia's capital. Operations at King Khalid International Airport, Saudi Arabia's second-busiest airport after Jeddah, were suspended to "allow for the completion of procedures to ensure the safety and operational readiness of the airport's facilities", the Saudi civil aviation authority said in a statement. Late on Monday, the Houthis said they had attacked the airport with a ballistic missile, shortly after Saudi Arabia said it had intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile fired by the group towards Riyadh.

items.title: IJM shares fall despite securing RM1.23 bln contruction contract in Kedah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: IJM Corporation Bhd shares fell in early trading today despite its unit securing a RM1.23 billion construction contract in Kedah. IJM's wholly-owned subsidiary, IJM Construction Sdn Bhd, has accepted a letter of award from AT&S Austria Technologie & Systemtechnik (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd for a design and build contract worth about RM1.23 billion. Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) said it views the contract win as a breakthrough for IJM in the semiconductor buildout space.

items.title: Bar Council tightens rules on lawyers handling clients' money
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Stricter rules will be imposed on law firms next year when handling clients' money following concerns over dishonest lawyers who have led to substantial insurance payouts. Under the new rules, law firms with more than one partner must get approval from two partners before making transactions involving clients' accounts. The changes are part of the Bar Council's 2027 Professional Indemnity Insurance (PII) scheme, which provides insurance protection to law firms against certain claims arising from their legal work.

items.title: Eco Discovery 2026 promotes Hulu Selangor's heritage, ecotourism
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Hulu Selangor Explorace: Eco Discovery 2026, held on Oct 10, drew an encouraging response from participants by focusing on ecotourism, environmental sustainability and social responsibility. MPHS president Julaihah Jamaludin said the positive response to the competition, held in Kuala Kubu Bharu, indicated strong public interest in exploring the district's unique history, heritage and natural beauty. "This also reflects growing interest in visiting Hulu Selangor to discover its unique history, heritage, natural beauty and other attractions," she said in a statement today.

items.title: Kelantan teacher claims trial over student's death, injury to another
items.summary: KOTA BARU: A female teacher has claimed trial in the magistrate's court to two counts of negligence resulting in the death of one student and injuries to another at Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Tanjong Mas in April. The accused, Sakinah Ismail, 57, pleaded not guilty after the charges were read before magistrate Wan Mohd I'zzat Wan Abdullah. Deputy public prosecutor Muhammad Nadzir Abdullah prosecuted, while lawyers Muhammad Hasif Hasan and Wan Fadhil Fayyadh Wan Mohd Zuhairi represented Sakinah.

items.title: MARKET PULSE AM OCT 13, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia's 30-stock index opened marginally lower, trailing Wall Street's mixed performance as oil prices hit its highest level in almost two weeks. The key index dropped one point, 3.9, to open at 1,616. E2z37RuiWuw © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Malaysia travellers gain new gateways to Europe and Central Asia via Vietjet
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian travellers will have more options to explore Europe and Central Asia as Vietjet expands its international network with new routes linking Hanoi to Almaty in Kazakhstan and Prague in the Czech Republic. The new services mark the airline's expansion into the European Union and strengthen air connectivity between Asia and Europe, with Malaysian passengers able to connect through Hanoi via Vietjet's direct flights from Kuala Lumpur. Vietjet chief executive officer Nguyen Thanh Son said the new routes marked an important milestone in the airline's international expansion.

items.title: Pasir Gudang logs country’s worst air quality at 181 API, 20 stations remain unhealthy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Air quality across Malaysia showed modest improvement this morning, with 20 of the country's 68 monitoring stations recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 10.40am, down from 23 stations reported yesterday afternoon. According to Department of Environment (DOE) surveillance data, 44 stations recorded moderate air quality, four registered good levels, and none breached the very unhealthy or hazardous thresholds. Readings between 101 and 200 fall within the unhealthy classification.

items.title: Is Malaysia’s fiscal health on the mend? BMI says yes in post-Budget forecast
items.summary: The Fitch Solutions unit said it expects the government to attain its 2027 revenue target of RM380.8 billion, a 4.7 per cent year-on-year (y-o-y) increase from the upward revised 2026 target of RM363.3 billion. “The Ministry of Finance had revised higher its 2026 growth projections to 4.8-5.3 per cent (BMI: 5.1 per cent) from 4.0-5.0 per cent previously. It expects growth to moderate to 4.2-5.2 per cent in 2027 (BMI: 4.5 per cent),” BMI said in a statement.

items.title: Steel prices climb 5.1pct, cement surges 7.4pct
items.summary: The department said the steel unit price index rose between 0.1 per cent and 5.1 per cent year-on-year (YoY), with Perak recording the steepest increase at 5.1 per cent, followed by Johor at 4.8 per cent and Tawau at 3.8 per cent. Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Melaka and Negri Sembilan recorded the highest annual increase in cement prices at 7.4 per cent, followed by Kuching at seven per cent and Miri at 6.6 per cent. Steel prices also retreated month-on-month, with the unit price index declining between 0.2 per cent and 1.6 per cent across selected areas.

items.title: IJM's RM1.23bil Kulim deal signals breakthrough in semiconductor manufacturing
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: IJM Corp Bhd's RM1.23 billion contract to build a semiconductor manufacturing facility in Kulim marks a breakthrough in its advanced manufacturing business, analysts said. He said IJM's in-house industrialised building system (IBS) capabilities likely played a key role in securing the contract, given the project's tight 14-month construction timeline. The contract was awarded to IJM Construction, a wholly-owned subsidiary of IJM, by Austria Technologie & Systemtechnik (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd (AT&S Malaysia).

items.title: Gang using Mercedes-Benz to steal TM cables in broad daylight busted
items.summary: SEREMBAN: A cable theft gang active in four states and recently filmed stealing Telekom Malaysia cables in broad daylight using a Mercedes-Benz and a pickup truck has been busted. Seremban police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Yatim Osman said the arrests had helped solve several cable theft cases in Negri Sembilan, Selangor, Kedah and Melaka. In the viral incident, four masked men using four vehicles, including a Mercedes-Benz and a pickup truck, were seen pulling cables from two TM manholes near a junction outside the school.

items.title: IMF upgrades 2026 growth forecast but warns of 'split' outlook
items.summary: BANGKOK: The International Monetary Fund on Tuesday forecast that global growth in 2026 would slow less than previously expected due to advanced economies' "resilience" in the face of war-fuelled energy prices but warned that low-income countries remained vulnerable to the supply shock. In its World Economic Outlook (WEO) released at the organisation's Annual Meetings in Bangkok, the Fund raised its 2026 global growth forecast by 0.1 percentage points to 3.1 per cent, compared to 3.5 per cent growth in 2025. The IMF warned that while many advanced economies have been buoyed by rising investment in artificial intelligence (AI) technology, poorer countries that are not benefiting from that boom face stark choices as they deal with high energy prices due to the US war on Iran.

items.title: In Dewan Rakyat today: Myanmar refugees, Gaza crisis, and minimum wage
items.summary: According to the Order Paper on Parliament’s official portal, during the Minister’s Question Time (MQT), Aminolhuda Hassan (PH-Sri Gading) will ask the Economy Minister to explain government mechanisms to ensure the minimum wage implementation does not result in job losses, price hikes, or increased operating costs for small enterprises. Jimmy Puah Wee Tse (PH-Tebrau) will ask the Home Minister about the target for registering Myanmar refugees over the next two years through the Refugee Registration Document (DPP) Programme, including targeted numbers and implementation timeline. Ahmad Tarmizi Sulaiman (PN-Sik) will ask the Foreign Minister to outline the government’s strategic steps following three years of genocide in Gaza, particularly in strengthening protection for Palestinians, humanitarian aid access, international accountability, and the reconstruction of Gaza.

items.title: French school shooting: Teenager fires four shots, wounds two teachers
items.summary: AUBAGNE: A 14-year-old boy opened fire with a hunting gun at a middle school in France on Monday, wounding the headmaster and a teacher before being disarmed by a member of staff, local authorities said. The shooting took place at Joseph-Lakanal middle school in the southern town of Aubagne, near Marseille, where a third person was grazed by gunfire, police said. "The middle school was not affected by the high school students' protest," police told AFP.

items.title: Malaysia's fiscal deficit to narrow, but spending risks persist: BMI
items.summary: The Fitch Solutions unit said it expects the government to attain its 2027 revenue target of RM380.8 billion, a 4.7 per cent year-on-year (y-o-y) increase from the upward revised 2026 target of RM363.3 billion. "The Ministry of Finance had revised higher its 2026 growth projections to 4.8-5.3 per cent (BMI: 5.1 per cent) from 4.0-5.0 per cent previously. It expects growth to moderate to 4.25.2 per cent in 2027 (BMI: 4.5 per cent)," BMI said in a statement.

items.title: RM510b but no new taxes? Amir Hamzah says 20227 Budget possible through cutting leakages
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The government is confident it can spend the RM510 billion allocated in Budget 2027 without introducing any new taxes, says Minister of Finance II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan. He said the government has always emphasised governance to reduce leakage and wastage in the current system to improve the efficiency of national spending. Amir Hamzah said the country’s continuously strengthening economic data reflects the confidence of foreign investors to keep investing in Malaysia, which in turn can generate national income.

items.title: Kinergy's RM47.5mil data centre contract to add RM1.4mil to net profit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Kinergy Advancement Bhd's RM47.5 million data centre contract is expected to contribute RM1.4 million to its net profit over the financial years ending 2026 (FY26) to FY28, said RHB Research. The research firm said the contract involves core and shell electrical infrastructure works for a data centre, with Kinergy Advancement expected to commence work by year-end and complete the project in the first quarter (Q1) of 2028. The research house maintained its "Buy" call on the stock with a target price of 60 sen, noting that the contract falls within its RM60 million new orderbook replenishment target for the engineering division.

items.title: Body wrapped in cloth found in Permatang Pauh market drain
items.summary: PERMATANG PAUH: A man's body, wrapped in cloth, was found in a drain at Sama Gagah Market here around 7am. Asma said she could not get a closer look at the body as police had cordoned off the area to facilitate investigations. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Unregistered Orang Asli in Malaysia: Why the NRD struggles to find accurate numbers
items.summary: GUA MUSANG, Oct 13 — The absence of accurate numbers of individuals without identification documents poses a challenge for the National Registration Department (NRD) in identifying the Orang Asli and indigenous communities who are still left out of the national registration system. He said that NRD is committed to implementing outreach programmes to engage with communities in rural areas, including providing services for first-time identity card applications, identity card replacements, as well as matters related to birth and death certificates. Badrul Hisham said that continuous efforts are important to ensure that communities in rural areas have access to documentation services, as well as to help address the issue of registration neglect among those communities.

items.title: Johor property back in focus as JS-SEZ plan, RTS lift investor confidence
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Johor's property market is poised for a defining moment, with the highly anticipated Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) masterplan and blueprint set to be unveiled this December. RHB Research said the move could unlock fresh value across Iskandar Malaysia and reinforce the region's position as a premier cross-border investment hub. "Despite the delay, the investment thesis for Iskandar Malaysia has not changed," Loong said in a recent note.

items.title: Kelana Jaya LRT Line trains diverted amid maintenance work
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Some Kelana Jaya Line LRT trains will be temporarily diverted due to ongoing maintenance work on several trains, Rapid KL said in a Facebook post today. It said the temporary service arrangement was intended to manage passenger flow at stations with higher demand. "Passengers are advised to take note of the changes and allow for extra travel time," it said.

items.title: UK shoppers stay cautious as fuel costs bite
items.summary: The British Retail Consortium (BRC) trade body said its total retail sales measure rose by 1.3 per cent compared with a year ago, picking up from 0.7 per cent in August but below its 12-month average of 1.5 per cent. A separate survey from Barclays, based on consumer card spending data, showed a 2.0 per cent annual increase in September, slowing from August's 2.1 per cent rise. • Barclays said essential spending was up by 2.5 per cent, driven by a 17.3 per cent jump in fuel spending after diesel prices hit record highs, while non-essential spending edged up by 1.8 per cent.

items.title: Man feared drowned after being swept away in Kajang’s Sungai Chuah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — A local man in his 40s is feared drowned after being reportedly swept away in Sungai Chuah, Kajang, Sunday. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) operations assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the search and rescue (SAR) operation, which began yesterday, was suspended at 4.30 pm yesterday due to heavy rain and will resume tomorrow. He said the search was carried out using kayaks and boats, alongside search efforts along the riverbanks.

items.title: Malaysia aims to slap ‘disaster’ status on transboundary haze at Asean meet
items.summary: SEPANG, Oct 13 — Malaysia will raise the issue of transboundary haze at an Asean foreign ministers’ meeting ahead of the bloc’s 49th Summit in Manila, the Philippines, next month to discuss more effective regional mechanisms to tackle the problem. Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said the haze issue required special attention as it was not covered by existing Asean mechanisms for natural disasters. On the latest efforts to extinguish fires in Indonesia, he said his counterpart, Arrmanatha Nasir, had informed him that extremely poor visibility in affected areas was hampering aerial firefighting operations.

items.title: MOH will push for absorbing contract dental and pharmacy officers, says Dzulkefly
items.summary: Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the proposal would be pursued within a reasonable timeframe, based on the approach previously used to address the issue of contract medical doctors. He said the recruitment of dental and pharmacy officers into permanent positions would utilise a new quota separate from the 9,000 permanent medical doctor positions announced under Budget 2027. The Malaysian Dental Association (MDA) was previously reported to have urged the government and MOH to consider permanent appointments for contract dental officers, following the announcement of permanent appointments for medical doctors.

items.title: Rusting away: Over 27,000 abandoned vehicles in Klang Valley
items.summary: Three local authorities in the Klang Valley recorded a total of 27,117 abandoned vehicles, based on records covering different periods from 2021 to August this year. Kajang Municipal Council recorded the highest number at 12,290 vehicles, followed by Kuala Lumpur City Hall with 11,001 complaints and Ampang Jaya Municipal Council with 3,826 vehicles. Abandoned vehicles can pollute soil and water through oil leaks and become breeding grounds for mosquitoes and pests.

items.title: 2027 Budget will boost digital ecosystem
items.summary: The initiatives aim to expand digital access, improve public services and boost economic competitiveness. Among the key initiatives are RM5 billion for the National Digital Network Plan (JENDELA), RM1 billion for the national digital healthcare ecosystem and RM142 million to strengthen National Information Dissemination Centres (NADI). The National Digital Healthcare Ecosystem and Connectivity Initiative (PERSADA) will improve digital infrastructure and connectivity in the healthcare sector.

items.title: Pack of eight stray dogs attacks child at Johor playground; Iskandar Puteri council launches raid
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Oct 13 — A seven-year-old boy was injured after being attacked by a pack of six to eight stray dogs while playing at a playground near a low-cost housing flat in Lima Kedai here yesterday. Kota Iskandar assemblyman Datuk Pandak Ahmad said the incident occurred between 3 pm and 4 pm, when the boy was believed to have been playing before the stray dogs attacked him, causing him to fall and roll on the ground as he tried to escape. he said.

items.title: Over 25,000 foreigners detained in crackdown on illegal businesses
items.summary: He said the operations comprised Op Belanja, targeting business and retail premises; Op Jaja, focusing on hawker activities; and Op Selera, targeting restaurants, eateries and food preparation premises. He said 5,173 operations were conducted under Op Belanja, involving inspections of 20,882 people, with a total of 5,809 undocumented migrants and 471 employers detained. Meanwhile, 6,603 Op Selera operations were conducted, involving inspections of 51,847 people.

items.title: Fury as US federal agents search anti-Trump lawmaker's home
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US federal agents searched the Washington home of Democratic congresswoman Ilhan Omar on Monday as part of what officials said was a criminal investigation, marking a dramatic escalation in President Donald Trump's confrontation with the outspoken lawmaker. Omar said she was "ok" following the operation but accused the administration of targeting political opponents just three weeks before she seeks re-election in the Nov 3 midterms. "Make no mistake: this is an attempt to target political enemies and weaponise federal law enforcement," Omar wrote on X.

items.title: Deputy minister warns ‘influencers’ against exploiting religious rituals for content
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Social media influencers have been reminded not to exploit issues involving race, religion and royalty (3R), particularly religious rituals, for online content, in the interest of preserving harmony in the country’s multiracial society. Deputy National Unity Minister R. Yuneswaran said influencers with large followings should be more responsible in producing content and spreading positive values instead of playing on 3R sentiments. Yuneswaran said the ministry viewed the issue involving religious rituals seriously and hoped it would be handled tactfully, adding that the investigation had been left entirely to the religious authorities and the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM).

items.title: Australia business confidence falls further in September amid oil price volatility
items.summary: SYDNEY: Australian business conditions were broadly unchanged in September, though confidence slipped further amid a surge in oil prices driven by renewed tensions in the Middle East, raising concerns over higher costs, a survey showed on Tuesday. The survey from National Australia Bank showed its index of business conditions was flat at -1 in September. However, the ongoing decline in confidence suggests that conditions will likely deteriorate further, the survey said.

items.title: Haze: 19 areas nationwide record unhealthy API readings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Nineteen areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 8am today, with Pasir Gudang in Johor recording the highest reading at 180. In Pahang, unhealthy readings were recorded in Balok Baru, Kuantan (161) and Rompin (157). In Negri Sembilan, Seremban recorded 154 and Nilai 146, while Tawau in Sabah recorded 154.

items.title: Higher minimum wage not a silver bullet, but crucial for income growth, says Johan Merican
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The implementation of the RM2,000 minimum wage next June is structured to provide businesses and corporations with an adequate transition window to adjust their salary frameworks, Treasury Secretary-General Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican said. Raising the minimum wage is part of that strategy. Alongside the RM2,000 statutory minimum wage and the RM3,400 GLC living wage threshold, Johan said the government will also maintain momentum on the Progressive Wage Policy, with plans also underway to introduce a dedicated minimum wage tier for semi-skilled occupations.

items.title: Malaysia is getting a new e-commerce law, what could change for online shoppers?
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Online shoppers could see clearer accountability for e-commerce platforms and sellers under a new law. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced when tabling Budget 2027 that the government had agreed to introduce a new law to replace Malaysia’s Electronic Commerce Act 2006. If passed by Parliament and brought into force, the proposed legislation would strengthen accountability among online platforms and sellers.

items.title: Firefly cancels Subang-Singapore flights until October 14 as haze persists
items.summary: SINGAPORE, Oct 12 — Prevailing weather and haze conditions have forced Firefly to extend flight cancellations between Subang and Singapore’s Seletar Airport until October 14, with affected passengers being offered alternative Malaysia Airlines flights, subject to seat availability, or full refunds. Firefly, a wholly owned subsidiary of Malaysia Airlines, had earlier cancelled all scheduled flights between Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport in Subang and Seletar Airport from October 10 to 12 as a precautionary safety measure. “Affected passengers are being contacted and reallocated onto available Malaysia Airlines services via the Kuala Lumpur-Singapore route, subject to seat availability.

items.title: Federal-state cooperation key to inclusive, sustainable development, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Close cooperation between the federal and state governments is essential to ensuring that national development is planned in an inclusive, sustainable and comprehensive manner for the benefit of the people. In a Facebook post, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he made the remarks while chairing the 51st National Physical Planning Council (MPFN) meeting in Putrajaya today. Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said the meeting reviewed various matters related to national physical development, including land-use planning and State Structure Plans, in line with the Town and Country Planning Act 1976 (Act 172).

items.title: Kedah police: Motorcycle theft allegation believed to have led to teen’s torture death
items.summary: Kedah police chief Datuk Adzli Abu Shah said police received information about the discovery of the body at 8.05am on October 8, while a post-mortem found that the victim had died from blunt force trauma to the head. Adzli said the victim was found dead inside the house on the night of October 7, and his body was subsequently dumped by the roadside. Police seized 14 mobile phones, a Honda City, scissors and the victim’s identity card.

items.title: Finance Ministry to strengthen oversight of public funds through amended Audit Act, new procurement law
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — The Finance Ministry will use amendments to the Audit Act 1957 and the Government Procurement Act 2026 to strengthen oversight of public funds and improve transparency in government spending. Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican said the amended Audit Act gives the Auditor-General greater scope to trace funds across government agencies and examine how the money is used. “The government has also approved the Government Procurement Act, which enables the government to tighten oversight in terms of transparency and value for money in the procurement process.

items.title: Malaysia targets 3.3pc fiscal deficit in 2027, 3pc by 2028, says Treasury sec-gen
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Malaysia is targeting a fiscal deficit of 3.3 per cent next year as it presses ahead with plans to bring the figure down to 3 per cent by 2028, Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican said today. Speaking at a panel discussion titled “Post-Budget 2027 Debate” organised by the Malaysian Economic Association in Kuala Lumpur, Johan said fiscal consolidation remained a key government priority, particularly in maintaining investor confidence. The government is targeting a fiscal deficit of 3.6 per cent this year, after reducing it from 5.5 per cent in 2022 to 3.7 per cent in 2025.

items.title: Seven-year-old seriously injured in Johor stray dog attack, teen escapes unhurt in earlier incident at same location
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Oct 12 — A seven-year-old boy suffered serious injuries after he was attacked by eight stray dogs while playing at a playground at a housing complex in Lima Kedai here today. Kota Iskandar assemblyman Datuk Pandak Ahmad expressed concern over the incident urging authorities to address the issue of stray dogs. Pandak said the incident involving the child was the second to occur today.

items.title: Govt aims to improve water quality in 33 polluted rivers in Malaysia by 10pc, says DPM Fadillah
items.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof said the target was set at the second 2026 meeting of the National Special Committee on Addressing River Water Quality Deterioration, which he chaired today. In Selangor, the Selangor Water Management Authority (Luas) reported 144 cases of water source pollution detected over the three years up to September 14, 2026, with varying levels of risk. Fadillah said polluted rivers could disrupt water treatment plant operations, affect public water supplies, increase treatment costs and affect economic activities, underscoring the need to make water resource protection a shared priority at all levels of administration.

items.title: Budget 2027: Pet vaccination, sterilisation eligible for tax relief
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — The government proposes expanding the scope of individual income tax relief for lifestyle to include pet care expenses, such as vaccinations and sterilisation treatments by registered veterinary services. MoF said the personal income tax relief cap for lifestyle remains at RM2,500, including the proposed expansion. Additionally, to promote digital literacy and the use of artificial intelligence (AI) technology to boost productivity and drive innovation, the scope of the personal income tax relief for lifestyle is proposed to be expanded to include subscription costs for AI software and applications for personal use, spouses, or children.

items.title: High Court allows MCMC’s preliminary objection, Papagomo committal hearing on Dec 23
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — The High Court will first hear the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission’s (MCMC) committal application against blogger Wan Muhammad Azri Wan Deris, also known as Papagomo, before proceeding with the inter-partes injunction hearing. “The court also extended the existing ad interim injunction against Wan Muhammad Azri until December 23. Therefore, MCMC has applied to the court for leave to commence a committal proceeding against Wan Azri.

items.title: Malaysia, Jordan seek high-tech cooperation to train more engineers, says Anwar
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 12 — Malaysia and Jordan are seeking to expand strategic cooperation in high-tech industries, particularly semiconductors and advanced technical education and training, to develop more engineers and skilled workers for future industry needs. “We also discussed potential cooperation in developing advanced technical education and training centres, including producing more engineers and skilled workers to meet future industry demands,” he posted on Facebook. Anwar said discussions also covered expanding trade and investment, including a potential free trade agreement (FTA), tariff restructuring, stronger supply chains and cooperation in energy, transport, the halal industry and tourism.

items.title: TNB confirms electrical accident at its installation in Johor’s Kota Tinggi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) has confirmed an electrical accident involving a member of the public at one of its installations in Kota Tinggi, Johor, today. In a statement posted on Facebook by TNB CareLine, the utility company said its technical team was dispatched to the location shortly after receiving a report of the incident. The company also advised the public against tampering with, opening or approaching electrical installations, warning that such actions could result in serious injury or death.

items.title: No need to replace old birth certificates, still valid, says NRD; new copies cost RM5
items.summary: GUA MUSANG, Oct 12 — Old birth certificates, including handwritten documents issued in paper format, remain valid and do not need to be replaced, said National Registration Department (NRD) director-general Datuk Badrul Hisham Alias. Badrul Hisham said birth documentation was essential to establish a legally recognised identity and ensure individuals could access their rights and services as Malaysians. He said the NRD continued to reach out to communities, including the Orang Asli in rural areas, to ensure they had access to registration and documentation services.

items.title: Kedah police bust online scam syndicate posing as Indian police officers
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Oct 12 — Kedah police successfully crippled an online scam syndicate involving suspects posing as Indian police officers during a raid on a business premises in Bandar Putra, Kulim, last Friday. Kedah Police Chief Datuk Adzli Abu Shah said that during the joint operation at 8pm, police arrested 48 individuals suspected of acting as syndicate members, comprising seven locals, eight Indian nationals, and 33 Pakistani nationals. “Additionally, police seized various items including 89 mobile phones, seven laptops, modems, monitors, Indian police uniforms, Indian flags, Indian Central Bureau of Investigation flags, and several other items.

items.title: Two killed, two injured in three-vehicle pile-up on Federal Highway
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Two men were killed while two others were injured in an accident involving three cars at Kilometer 18.2 of the Federal Highway heading towards Kuala Lumpur, early this morning. Petaling Jaya District Police Chief ACP Shamsudin Mamat said the accident, which occurred at approximately 12.20am, involved a Proton Wira driven by a local man in his 20s who was travelling from Shah Alam to Kuala Lumpur. Shamsudin said the Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division of the Petaling Jaya District Police Headquarters received a report regarding the fatal accident at 1:05 am today.

items.title: Opposition leader criticises GLC involvement in non-core projects in Budget 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Opposition Leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin today alleged that government-linked corporations (GLCs) were being made to operate beyond their core mandates. While debating Budget 2027, he cited a project to build a hostel for students that he said would be funded by the Retirement Fund Incorporated (KWAP), alleging this practice extended to others such as Petronas, Tenaga Nasional Bhd, and more. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim tabled a record RM459 billion federal spending plan for 2027 last Friday, in which he also outlined a RM50 billion from government-linked investment companies, state enterprises and statutory bodies.

items.title: 1MDB in talks to settle lawsuit with Deutsche Bank
items.summary: 1MDB’s counsel, Datuk Lim Chee Wee, informed the Federal Court of the settlement talks during proceedings today before a three-member panel led by Chief Judge of Malaya Datuk Seri Hashim Hamzah. The panel, comprising Chief Judge of Sabah and Sarawak Datuk Seri Azizah Nawawi and Federal Court Judge Datuk Ravinthran N. Paramaguru, was hearing 1MDB’s application for leave to appeal against a decision in favour of UK law firm White & Case LLP. The hearing for that case is scheduled for October 26 before High Court Judicial Commissioner Rihada Rafie,” Lim said.
